title: When the Wolf Sings
premise: Lior Thackeray, an exiled storm-caller hiding as a charm-seller in the magic-free city of Vell, discovers their face in a century-old prophecy book that names them the Wolf-Singer—the one destined to either free or destroy the storm-bound north. Hunted by the usurper Kaelen Voss's inquisitors and pursued by a resistance faction that wants to weaponize them, Lior must embrace the inherited power they fled seven years ago. The prophecy's final verse reveals Lior's own mother wrote it, sacrificing herself to seal the ancient war; in the end, Lior chooses neither conquest nor erasure, breaking the cycle by unbinding the storm-magic from bloodlines entirely—at the cost of their own gift and their place in any world, human or magical.
about_author: Astrid Crane is the pen name of a former folklorist who spent a decade collecting storm songs along northern coastlines before turning to fiction. Their debut novel draws on those field recordings and the oral traditions of exile communities.

chapters.title: Charms for a City Without Magic
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. In rain-soaked Vell, Lior sells harmless trinkets disguised as charms, carefully performing powerlessness while suppressing the storm humming under their skin. A routine sale to a nervous scholar plants unease. Emotional beat: the exhausting loneliness of a life built on concealment.

chapters.title: The Date That Was Written
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The scholar returns with a cracked leather codex—prophecies penned a century ago—and shows Lior a passage describing tonight: a stranger with storm-grey eyes selling a copper bell. The date matches. Emotional beat: vertigo as invisibility collapses into destiny.

chapters.title: What the Codex Calls Them
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, with the scholar Maren. Reading deeper, they find the title 'Wolf-Singer' and a verse about a war sealed in blood. Lior burns the page and lies to Maren—but the city watch has already been tipped off. Emotional beat: fear curdling into denial.

chapters.title: Inquisitor's Lantern
chapters.summary: Sergeant Odile Vane's POV. A zealous inquisitor arrives in Vell carrying warrants for a 'storm-caller of Thackeray line.' Odile, who has quietly protected Lior for years, must decide what loyalty means. Emotional beat: dread of the law arriving where friendship lived.

chapters.title: Seven Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Lior's POV. The night of exile: Lior's uncontrolled magic killed their mentor during a rite of inheritance, and their mother's last words—'never sing'—sent them south. Emotional beat: guilt revealed as the true prison, not the banishment.

chapters.title: The Bell Rings Anyway
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Cornered in the market, Lior's suppressed magic erupts involuntarily when the inquisitor seizes Maren—a thunderclap levels a street. They flee together into the undercity. Emotional beat: terror at one's own power, and the end of hiding.

chapters.title: Beneath Vell
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. In the smuggler tunnels, Maren reveals she is a courier for the Free Cities Compact, hunting the codex itself. She offers Lior sanctuary—and use. Emotional beat: wary hope tangled with the suspicion of being wanted only as a weapon.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Road
chapters.summary: Kaelen Voss's POV. The usurper marches on the free cities, wielding captured storm-priests as living artillery. He knows the Wolf-Singer lives and wants them found first. Emotional beat: cold ambition; the antagonist shown as corruption wearing a crown of necessity.

chapters.title: Salt and Ashes
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The road north through burned villages shows what Voss's armies leave behind. Lior heals a dying child with a thread of storm-light—the first deliberate magic in seven years. Emotional beat: grief transmuting into resolve.

chapters.title: The Compact's Bargain
chapters.summary: Lior and Maren's POV alternating. At the fortress-city of Harrowgate, Compact leaders offer protection in exchange for Lior leading a counterstrike. Lior hesitates; Maren argues both sides of her conscience. Emotional beat: belonging offered at the price of autonomy.

chapters.title: Songs in the Old Tongue
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Studying the codex with Harrowgate's archivist, Lior realizes the prophecies are written in their family's private cipher—the author is kin. A hidden map points to the drowned abbey of Vaelmoor. Emotional beat: wonder shading into suspicion of the prophecy's true purpose.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Toll
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile, tracking Lior to warn them, uncovers a Compact officer selling their route to Voss. Her warning arrives too late—an ambush at the river crossing scatters the party. Emotional beat: betrayal, and Odile choosing exile over duty.

chapters.title: Drowned Abbey
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. In Vaelmoor's flooded cloisters, Lior finds their mother's tomb and her true journal: she authored the prophecy to guide—not doom—her child, sealing the old war with her own life. Emotional beat: mourning rewritten as inheritance of choice, not curse.

chapters.title: The First Verse Fulfilled
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Voss's vanguard strikes Harrowgate using the stolen route; the city falls in a night. Maren survives to carry word north, hating that her recruitment of Lior made it possible. Emotional beat: guilt and the collapse of easy alliances.

chapters.title: Wolf-Singer
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Refugees gather around Lior after they call down a storm to break a Voss patrol. The legend takes hold whether Lior wills it or not; followers begin calling them Wolf-Singer. Emotional beat: the seduction and horror of being believed in.

chapters.title: The Corruption of Crowns
chapters.summary: Kaelen Voss's POV. Voss offers Lior a parley: join him and the free cities are spared. He reveals he too was once a storm-caller who chose control over chaos—and shows what Lior could become. Emotional beat: temptation rendered genuinely reasonable.

chapters.title: The Parley at Greyford Bridge
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The parley collapses when Compact hardliners ambush Voss, hoping to martyr their cause. Lior saves Voss from assassination, shattering both sides' plans. Emotional beat: moral clarity purchased at the cost of every alliance.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Free Cities
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. Voss's full army advances; the Compact fractures between fighting and surrendering. Lior, armed with their mother's journal, proposes a third path: unbind storm-magic from bloodlines at the source—the Wellspring beneath Vaelmoor. Emotional beat: desperate clarity before the endgame.

chapters.title: The Last Verse
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. The journal's final page warns the unbinding requires the singer's own gift—and possibly their life—as the price. Lior says goodbye to Maren and Odile without telling them everything. Emotional beat: quiet acceptance; love expressed through concealment.

chapters.title: Vaelmoor Rises
chapters.summary: Climax, Lior's POV. As armies collide outside, Lor descends into the Wellspring, singing the unbinding while Voss fights through to stop them—wanting the magic for himself. The storm answers Lior's song one last time. Emotional beat: transcendence amid ruin.

chapters.title: After the Thunder
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The unbinding ripples outward: Voss's weaponized priests are freed, his army dissolves, and he falls—powerless, ordinary. Lior emerges alive but hollowed, their gift gone. Emotional beat: victory that feels like bereavement.

chapters.title: A Charm-Seller Again
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, epilogue. Months later, Lior keeps a small stall in rebuilt Vell, selling honest trinkets with no magic left to hide. Maren visits; Odile sends letters; the codex is archived, its last verse blank. Emotional beat: peace earned—belonging chosen rather than prophesied.
